stem:
Zubin marks point $R$ above a flat floor. He drops a perpendicular from $R$ to the floor, meeting it at $H$. He also draws a slanted segment from $R$ to another floor point $K$.

Which claim correctly describes the perpendicular projection of $R$ onto the floor?

options.text: The foot $H$ is the perpendicular projection of $R$ onto the floor.
Name the answer as plane only, with no choice between $H$ and $K$.
Point $K$ is the projection because $K$ is farther along the floor from under $R$.
Any point on the floor is the projection of $R$, even when the joining segment is not perpendicular.

teacher.key_rationale: The perpendicular projection of a point onto a plane (here the floor) is the foot of the perpendicular from the point to the plane, so H is the projection, not slanted K.
